statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, r is the least positive integer k such that there exist k positive deci-binary integers a_1, ..., a_k with a_1 + ... + a_k = N(n), where N(n) is the integer represented in decimal by n, N(n) = sum over i from 0 to len(n)-1 of (n[i]-48) * 10^(len(n)-1-i), and a positive deci-binary integer means a positive integer whose usual decimal representation has no leading zero and every digit is either 0 or 1.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48, so n has no leading zero and represents a positive integer.

statement: The call min_partitions(n) returns a result; it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or any other panic.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, r = maxDigit(n), where maxDigit(n) = max { n[i]-48 | 0 <= i < len(n) }.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, 1 <= r <= 9.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i]-48 <= r.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(n) such that n[i]-48 = r.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, there exist r positive deci-binary integers a_1, ..., a_r, not necessarily distinct, such that a_1 + ... + a_r = N(n), where N(n) = sum over i from 0 to len(n)-1 of (n[i]-48) * 10^(len(n)-1-i), and deci-binary means usual decimal representation with no leading zero and all digits in {0,1}.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, for every integer k with 1 <= k < r there do not exist k positive deci-binary integers b_1, ..., b_k such that b_1 + ... + b_k = N(n), where N(n) is the integer represented by n and deci-binary means usual decimal representation with no leading zero and all digits in {0,1}.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if every digit of n is 0 or 1, i.e. for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] = 48 or n[i] = 49.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns a result r, r = 9 if and only if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(n) such that n[i]-48 = 9.
preconditions: len(n) is an integer with 1 <= len(n) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i] is the ASCII code of a decimal digit, i.e. 48 <= n[i] <= 57; and n[0] != 48.

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns r and min_partitions(m) returns r', we have r' >= r.
preconditions: n satisfies: len(n) is between 1 and 99999, every n[i] is an ASCII digit 48..57, and n[0] != 48. c is a byte with 48 <= c <= 57. m is the slice of length len(n)+1 defined by m[i]=n[i] for 0 <= i < len(n) and m[len(n)]=c; consequently len(m) <= 100000, every m[i] is an ASCII digit 48..57, and m[0]=n[0] != 48, so m has no leading zero.

statement: If for every i with 0 <= i < len(n), n[i]-48 <= m[i]-48, then whenever min_partitions(n) returns r_n and min_partitions(m) returns r_m, r_n <= r_m.
preconditions: Both n and m satisfy: lengths are between 1 and 100000, all entries are ASCII digits 48..57, and the first entry is not 48; additionally len(n) = len(m).

statement: Whenever min_partitions(n) returns r_n and min_partitions(m) returns r_m, r_n = r_m.
preconditions: n satisfies: len(n) is between 1 and 100000, every n[i] is an ASCII digit 48..57, and n[0] != 48. Also m satisfies the same byte constraints, len(m)=len(n), m[0] != 48, and for every digit value d in 0..9, the number of indices i with n[i]-48=d equals the number of indices i with m[i]-48=d.
